story.headline: Strong US figures, above all a big jump in consumer confidence, lifted the dollar to a near two-week high before Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, while oil slipped as talks with Iran went on.

reads.policy: Five central banks decide in the next four days, and most still lean toward raising rates because energy keeps inflation high. Strong US figures today made a December Fed hike look more likely, which helped the dollar. New Zealand goes first tonight, with Canada and the Fed on Wednesday.
reads.growth: The US economy keeps beating expectations: households are more upbeat and business orders are rising. In France, consumer mood sank to a 13-year low. That gap between a strong US and a soft euro area favours the dollar over the euro.
reads.inflation: Energy is still pushing inflation above target in most big economies, and it is spreading into shop prices in Britain and into underlying prices in Japan. American households still expect prices to rise quickly. That keeps central banks leaning toward hikes; Australia's inflation figures tonight are the next big reading.
reads.risk: Markets were calm: US stocks rose, led by big tech, and oil eased as talks with Iran went on. That cut demand for safe havens, so the yen and franc slipped. A failed round of talks or a confirmed hit on Saudi oil would quickly reverse that.
reads.tot: Oil slipped as talks with Iran continued, though attacks in the Gulf keep most of the war premium in the price. Cheaper oil is a small relief for energy importers like Japan and the euro area and a small loss for Canada.
reads.positioning: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar and the kiwi, even though both central banks are expected to hike this week, so those bets are exposed if the hikes come with signals of more. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.
reads.fiscal: Britain's first Budget from Chancellor John Healey lands on Wednesday morning, and heavier borrowing could unsettle UK bonds and the pound. In France, the budget vote slipped again and consumer gloom deepened, which keeps a weight on the euro.

fed.summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold rates on Wednesday and raise them in December, because high oil keeps US inflation near 3.7%. Strong US figures today made that December hike look more likely, which supports the dollar.
fed.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
fed.why: Energy-driven inflation is still well above the Fed's goal, and the economy keeps beating expectations, with households more upbeat and still expecting prices to rise quickly.
fed.watch: The decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday and Fed chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 1:30 PM CT. A hold is priced; the surprise would be a clear push toward or away from a December hike, or officials voting for a hike now.

boc.summary: The Bank of Canada is expected to raise rates on Wednesday because energy has pushed inflation above its forecasts. A hike would support the loonie; some big banks still expect a hold.
boc.priced: October: hike likely, but a hold is possible.
boc.why: Energy and import costs are lifting Canadian prices faster than the bank expected, even though US tariffs keep the economy soft.
boc.watch: The decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday and Governor Tiff Macklem's press conference. A hold would be the surprise; a hike with a signal of more would be the stronger outcome for the loonie.

rbnz.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is widely expected to raise its rate to 3% tonight, CT, because inflation is still above its target band. That has kept the kiwi firm.
rbnz.why: Inflation has cooled but remains above the bank's target band, and the services sector keeps growing, giving the bank room to tighten.
rbnz.watch: The decision at 8:00 PM CT tonight, and whether the bank signals more hikes after this one.

ecb.summary: The European Central Bank is expected to hold on Thursday and raise rates in December, because energy keeps euro-area inflation high. France's debt troubles and gloomy French households limit how much that helps the euro.
ecb.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
ecb.why: Energy costs keep inflation well above the bank's 2% goal, while growth is slowing and France's budget fight adds risk.
ecb.watch: The decision at 8:15 AM CT Thursday and President Christine Lagarde's press conference, especially anything on French bonds or a December hike.

boj.summary: The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on Friday and raise rates in December. Underlying inflation in Japan is now at a three-year high, but rates are still far below other major economies', which keeps the yen weak.
boj.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
boj.why: Inflation is broadening beyond energy, with the bank's own underlying gauge at a three-year high, which builds the case for a hike.
boj.watch: Tokyo consumer prices on Wednesday evening, CT, then the decision and new forecasts on Friday, Japan time. Any move by Tokyo to buy yen would also matter.

rba.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia may raise rates again on November 3, and markets see it as a coin toss. Tonight's inflation figures will likely decide it.
rba.priced: November: roughly even odds of a hike.
rba.why: Officials have said the inflation outlook has got worse, partly because of high oil, and the bank has kept its leaning toward more hikes.
rba.watch: Australia's third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT tonight: a core reading at or above what banks expect makes a November hike likely.

boe.summary: The Bank of England is all but certain to raise rates on November 5 because UK inflation is running hot. That supports the pound, though Wednesday's Budget is the near-term risk.
boe.priced: November: hike all but certain; December: a second hike possible.
boe.why: UK inflation is well above target, and shop prices are now rising at their fastest pace in two and a half years as energy costs spread.
boe.watch: Chancellor John Healey's Budget at about 7:30 AM CT Wednesday: how much the government borrows and spends feeds into the bank's next steps.

snb.summary: The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero because Swiss inflation is near zero, and markets are split on its next step. That leaves the franc relying on its role as a safe place for money.
snb.priced: December: markets split; no move is the slight favourite.
snb.why: Inflation is near zero, so the bank has no reason to hike, and it has grown more relaxed about a weaker franc.
snb.watch: Any comment on the franc from board members, and the December 10 decision.

USD.summary: The dollar has among the highest rates of the major currencies, with a Federal Reserve hike expected in December. Strong US figures lifted it to a near two-week high before Wednesday's Fed decision.

notes.policy: The Fed is expected to hold on Wednesday and hike in December, which supports the dollar.
notes.inflation: High oil keeps US inflation well above the Fed's goal, and households still expect prices to rise quickly.

EUR.summary: The euro is held back by weak euro-area growth, France's debt troubles and heavy energy costs, though an expected ECB hike in December helps. It has fallen five days in a row.

notes.policy: The ECB is expected to hold this week, so its December hike offers less near-term lift than rivals' moves.
notes.growth: Euro-area business surveys missed in October, and French consumer confidence fell to its lowest since 2013.
notes.inflation: Energy keeps euro-area inflation high, which keeps a December ECB hike on the table.
notes.tot: The euro area imports most of its energy, so high oil drains money out of the region.
notes.positioning: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the euro in years, which can fuel sharp rises if the news improves.
notes.fiscal: France's debt and budget fight weigh on the euro, and its budget vote has slipped again.

GBP.summary: The pound is supported by a Bank of England hike that is all but certain for November 5 and by hot inflation, but caution before Wednesday's UK Budget is holding it back.

notes.policy: A Bank of England hike on November 5 is all but priced, which supports the pound.
notes.growth: UK business surveys and a recent retail survey were better than feared.
notes.inflation: UK inflation is well above target, and shop prices are rising at their fastest in two and a half years.

JPY.summary: The yen sits low on the board because Japan's rates are still far below others' and the country pays for costly imported energy. A December Bank of Japan hike is widely expected, and Tokyo has warned it may act to support the yen.

notes.policy: Japan's rates are still well below other major economies', so holding yen pays little.
notes.risk: The yen gains when markets get nervous, but rising stocks have taken that support away.
notes.tot: Japan imports nearly all its energy, so oil near its highest since spring weighs on the yen.

CHF.summary: The franc is pulled between near-zero Swiss inflation, which keeps rates at zero, and its role as a safe place for money when markets are nervous.

notes.inflation: Swiss inflation is near zero, which leaves the Swiss National Bank no reason to raise rates.
notes.risk: The franc gains when investors look for safety, so calmer markets take some of that support away.

AUD.summary: The Aussie is supported by a central bank that may hike again in November, but weak business surveys hold it back. Australia's inflation figures tonight, CT, will likely decide its next move.

notes.policy: The Reserve Bank of Australia may raise rates on November 3, which supports the Aussie.
notes.growth: Australia's private sector shrank in October for the first time in five months, and unemployment is at a five-year high.
notes.tot: Australia exports energy and raw materials, so high commodity prices bring money into the country.

CAD.summary: The loonie is near its strongest in a month on a likely Bank of Canada hike this Wednesday and high oil, though US tariffs remain a headwind.

notes.policy: A Bank of Canada hike on Wednesday is mostly expected, which supports the loonie.
notes.growth: Canada's economy is still soft, and US tariffs weigh on its exporters.
notes.inflation: Energy and import costs are pushing Canadian inflation above the central bank's forecasts.
notes.tot: As an oil exporter, Canada gains from high oil prices, which remain near their highest since spring.

NZD.summary: The kiwi sits near the top of the board because New Zealand's central bank is expected to raise rates tonight, CT, and its services sector keeps growing.

notes.policy: A Reserve Bank of New Zealand hike is widely expected tonight, CT, which supports the kiwi.
notes.growth: New Zealand's services sector has grown for four straight months, giving the central bank room to raise rates.
notes.risk: The kiwi has held firm this month on the rate-hike bets, though it still drops when stocks fall.
notes.tot: Firm dairy prices, New Zealand's biggest export, bring money into the country.
